findings.message: The Medium-severity coupling-risk mitigation now states the write-partitioning contract in prose (mapping written once, never rewritten by the increment path, which uses an isolated partial-field write) — the substance the iteration-1 finding asked for — but anchors it on decision element ADR.01.03.5536 ("Write paths are partitioned per ADR.01.03.5536") that is never defined anywhere in the record. §3 Decision semantics define only ADR.01.03.5c3c, f5f5, 3315, 1050, and §6 adds 0db1. This dangling element reference is the load-bearing primitive that keeps a count-write fault off the redirect path (BDD.01.03.5f58/a7ad); a SPEC author following the citation to find the partitioning decision lands on nothing and must infer whether a formal partitioning commitment exists beyond the inline prose.
findings.recommendation: Either promote the partitioning primitive to a real decision element in §3 Decision (e.g., add 'ADR.01.03.5536 — Write-path partitioning: the durable mapping (original_url, status) is written once on issuance and never rewritten by the off-path increment, which performs an isolated partial-field write') and keep the §5 citation, or drop the ID from §5 and let the inline prose stand alone. Do not leave a citation pointing to an undefined element.

notes: Iter-1 write-ordering gap resolved in prose; fixer introduced a dangling ADR.01.03.5536 reference on the key coupling mitigation. Decision otherwise implementable, upstream-consistent, and cross-ADR-consistent (one-way exemption satisfies C4).
